answer: Agent-native Sybil resistance is formalized by coupling a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function with a high-value staking collateral to ensure a negative expected attack utility. This mechanism forces a sequential temporal cost that no adversary can forge via parallelization, effectively turning the identity layer into a rigid jetty against mass-spawned nodes. By applying slashing penalties to any identity attempting to reuse a jade-standard cryptographic seed, the system maintains a robust Nash equilibrium where the cost of identity proliferation exceeds potential rewards.
